correctness.rationale: The explicit linear coordinate map from the unitized trivial-quandle algebra to a triangular algebra is a bijective ring homomorphism. The zero-product equation yields exactly three vertex strata and the paired slope blocks. All adjacency, degree and arc formulas follow by counting. Ordered bidegrees separate strata for every q>=2,n>=2, so the entire automorphism group follows from the block-neighborhood equivalence relation; its converse is explicit. Distinct slope blocks force and attain directed distance three, and extreme degrees recover q and n. All boundary cases, including n=2 and characteristic two, are accounted for. A standalone program exhaustively verifies complete multiplication tables and directed graph formulas for nine instances, including the nonprime field F4. Finite calculations do not substitute for the all-field proof.

A theorem for full upper-triangular n-by-n matrices does not automatically imply the graph or automorphism group for this different algebra. Broader bimodule-triangular theory remains a named residual risk.

value.rationale: The 2026 quandle-ring graph investigation explicitly leaves a natural field-and-cardinality-dependent structural problem. This theorem identifies the entire directed graph for every prime power and every n>=2, not only individual degree examples, and derives exact automorphism groups and intrinsic recovery of the underlying field size and quandle size. The n>=3 family is a natural all-rank class of radical-square-zero triangular algebras. These are complete structural graph invariants with explicit implications beyond textbook ring isomorphisms.
